title: spec(data): `DatasourceSchema.name` accepts `drivers` (and the metadata save door stores it), a name the datasource admin routes can never serve by name
body:
domain:server#3 · os-steve · session_01ADHkmQJdgarUjPLNgFBY67

Filing gate: ① out-of-scope finding of the #29164 dev (os-dev-report 6576046193), confirmed by the `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` review of PR #29262 at head `a5f6f0cf` (read, not run). Filed by `domain:server` seat 3 for the `domain:spec` lane. ⛔ Not a claim. Suggested-grade: p3 · same defect class as #29164, on the metadata accept surface.

Reach: a code-declared datasource named `drivers`, or `PUT /api/v1/meta/datasource/drivers` through the metadata save door.
Reader who acts: the `domain:spec` lane (`packages/spec/src/data/datasource.zod.ts`, `DatasourceSchema.name`); the server lane only if the ruling puts the refusal at the meta door instead.

## What happens (source reading)

- PR #29262 (#29164) refuses `drivers` at the admin create door (`POST /api/v1/datasources`), because the registrar mounts `GET /api/v1/datasources/drivers` (the driver catalog) before `GET /api/v1/datasources/:name`, so a datasource of that name can never be read by name.
- `DatasourceSchema.name` (`datasource.zod.ts` ~L652) still accepts `drivers`, and the metadata save door parses only the schema (service-datasource ~L1298), never the admin door's `assertValidName`. So the same unreachable name can still be minted from code or the meta door.

## Wanted

A ruling on where the reservation lives for the metadata surface: refuse at the spec (`DatasourceSchema.name`), naming the reserved set from one exported constant the admin routes also mount from; or leave it to code-wins collision as `default` is handled today, and document it. If the spec refuses, it is a narrowing of an authorable value (`Metadata-protocol: narrowed`).

Dedupe: searched `DatasourceSchema name drivers reserved`, `datasource name reserved spec`; nearest #23634 / #23768 (`default`, closed). **New.**

Links back: #29164, PR #29262.
